RUN 2 -- mix letflow.check.test (the stricter ISS-0069 gate this role is separately required to run; not merely scripts/test_parallel.sh or a targeted mix test), foreground, synchronous, fully captured to a local log (no tail truncation) and blocked on to completion via a PID-liveness loop in the same turn: main suite N=16 again -- identical partition-14 signature reproduced a second, independent time (partition 14: 239 tests, 0 properties, 2 failures, exit 2; every other partition 0 failures), same two named tests (resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 / resolve_realm_by_tenant/1, Letflow.IdentityTest). `mix letflow.check.test` raises on the runner's nonzero exit before ever reaching its own ISS-0069 substring check (confirmed by reading lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex's check_main_suite_logs/2 ordering) -- grepped the full captured log directly regardless: zero occurrences of "default values for the optional arguments" anywhere. So this run's only failure, under both the plain parallel runner and the stricter check.test gate, is the identical pre-existing pair -- no ISS-0069-class regression, no new failure class.

STRUCTURAL ATTRIBUTION (re-derived independently, not inherited from TEST-RUNNER's claim): Route 1 -- `git diff --name-only main...HEAD` for this branch touches only lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex, lib/letflow/api/error.ex, lib/letflow/api/response.ex, lib/letflow/repository/attachment_links.ex, lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex, plus this run's own test/spec/design/handoff/status files -- grepped all five changed lib/ files myself for idp_realm_id/bpm-default/resolve_tenant_by_realm/resolve_realm_by_tenant: zero matches; none of test/letflow/identity_test.exs, test/support/bpm_default_realm_displacement.ex, or any Letflow.Identity/Tenant module is touched. Route 3 -- read docs/issues/ISS-0766.yaml in full myself: it already documents this exact failure signature (same file, same two test names, same mechanism -- an advisory-lock-scoped read racing a concurrent displace!/0 restoration under shared Postgres state across parallel partitions), and its own process_note (added 2026-09-21 by a prior RELEASE-VALIDATOR run) already records that this reproduces under scripts/test_parallel.sh's own partitioned method too, not just a non-partitioned run -- which is exactly what both of my independent runs (same partition-14 signature, twice) just re-confirmed as a live, demonstrated mechanism, not an assertion. Verdict: pre-existing, does not block this step's PASS, not routed back to ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-DESIGNER, not filed as a new issue (ISS-0766 already covers it exactly).

AC1 -- read lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex's handle_issue_attachment_link/3 (L1244-1264) directly: :AttachmentsRead-scoped authz_post route, reuses fetch_scoped_attachment_metadata/3 to prove access before minting, calls AttachmentLinks.issue/3. Request a new link and try again." is a plain-language literal, no interpolation. Confirmed AC2's route-level test ("AC2: ... expired token" describe block) uses AttachmentLinks.issue/3's injected now: option (already-past DateTime) rather than a real sleep -- grepped the test file myself for Process.sleep: zero hits. The unit-level attachment_links_test.exs also injects now: directly into verify/3 per case (confirmed by reading it).
AC3 -- req386_attachment_links_routes_test.exs's "AC3: fresh link after a prior one expired" test (read in full, L255-292) exercises stale-token-410 then a fresh POST (200) then a fresh GET (200, real bytes) in sequence, all against the same attachment_id.
AC4 -- the hardest criterion, re-derived myself from lib/letflow/repository/attachment_links.ex's verify/3 (L133-155): traced all 8 branches of the with/else chain (malformed-shape split, two Base64 decode failures, guarded Jason.decode/1 shape failure, unknown tenant, wrong/unresolvable per-tenant signing key, HMAC mismatch via :crypto.hash_equals/2, expiry) -- every branch falls to the single `else _ -> {:error, :expired_or_invalid}` clause; confirmed the token payload carries no tenant field at all (only attachment_id/expires_at/key_id, L102-107/141-143) so verify/3 always resolves the signing key under the CALLER's own tenant_id, never one decoded from the token -- this is what makes a cross-tenant-presented token fail identically to a fabricated one. Read the AC4 test in req386_attachment_links_routes_test.exs (L301-389) directly: it mints a REAL, validly-signed, unexpired token for tenant_1 via AttachmentLinks.issue/3, then presents that genuine token as tenant_2's caller against (a) tenant_2's own real different attachment_id and (b) a wholly fabricated never-issued UUID -- a genuine cross-tenant construction, not two independently-invalid tokens. Asserts status, content-type header, AND full resp_body byte-for-byte equality between the two responses, with no normalization applied (both conns share the harness's fixed "fixed-test-trace-id", so there is nothing to normalize away) -- matches req212_attachments_routes_test.exs's own established byte-identical-comparison precedent.
AC5 -- `git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex` shows fetch_scoped_attachment_content/3 is not touched at all (confirmed by grepping the diff for its name: it appears only in a comment and as an unchanged call site in the new handler, never inside a `+`/`-` line touching its own definition); read its current body directly (L1175-1195) and it is byte-for-byte the same shape REQ-211/212 shipped. `git diff --stat main...HEAD -- test/letflow/routers/req212_attachments_routes_test.exs test/letflow/repository/attachments_test.exs` is empty (confirmed myself) -- both files untouched -- and both are part of the two independent full-suite runs above with zero failures.
AC6 -- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (mine, this run): clean.
